title: Edge Config Constellation - proto notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for an experimental API/config proto that lets a fleet of edge runners form a lightweight ‘constellation’ for coordinated pre-warm, config distribution, and graceful fallback to private or hosted backends. Not a final spec — lots of open questions.

Context / motivation:
- We have multiple feature needs that push beyond simple per-runner config: coordinated cache warming, cross-runner KV hinting, lease-based shard handoff, and cross-tenant fallback graphs.
- Existing ingress + runtime bindings are too heavyweight for small edge pools (10-50 devices) where churn and network intermittency are common.
- Want a single minimal wire contract that:
  * expresses runner capabilities (gpu/cpu, quant profiles, token window),
  * encodes routing hints (preferred upstream, fallback chains),
  * supports live rollouts and canary signals,
  * includes a tiny control plane for leases and pre-warm directives.

High-level sketch (ASCII network view):

  [Controller] <---(manifest+rollout)--- [Edge Constellation Broker] --- multicast ---> {r1, r2, r3}
                                      |                                   |    |    |
                                      |                                   V    V    V
                                      |                                [r1]  [r2]  [r3]
                                      |                                  |     |     |
                                      '----(telemetry + lease heartbeats)-'     |     |
                                                                           (cache sync, prewarm commands)

Design goals / constraints:
- Minimal JSON-over-HTTP/HTTP2 + optionally gRPC for richer telemetry.
- Most operations are declarative manifests pushed from Controller -> Broker -> Runners.
- Runners must be able to operate offline for short windows; manifest changes are versioned and delta-patched.
- Backwards-compat via capability flags and small contract to avoid full negotiation.

Core message primitives (proto-ish, but expressed as shapes):

1) RunnerAdvertise (what a runner announces)
- id: string (runner-uuid)
- capabilities: [string] e.g. ["cuda:8gb", "quant-a16", "kv-cache-v1"]
- preferred_upstream: string (optional) e.g. "private-cluster-a"
- weight_hint: number (0-100)
- active_manifests: [manifest_id] (last-applied)
- heartbeat_ts: iso8601

2) Manifest (control plane unit)
- id: string (manifest-2026-02-10-abc)
- seq: number (monotonic)
- targets: selector (see below)
- directives: [directive] where directive is one of:
    * prewarm: {model: string, warm_tokens: number, quant_profile: string}
    * route_hint: {upstream: string, fallback_chain: [string]}
    * kv_patch: {patch_id: string, operations: [put/delete]}
- rollout: {strategy: "canary"|"rolling"|"immediate", percent: number}
- created_by: string
- created_ts: iso8601

3) Lease (short-lived ownership for shard / cache)
- lease_id: string
- owner: runner-id
- resource: string e.g. "kv-shard-3" or "prefetch-slot-1"
- ttl_seconds: number
- token: string (signed)

Selectors (very compact):
- allow simple selectors: "tag:gpu and not tag:old-quant" or "id:runner-12"
- encoded as small expression strings to keep proto size down

Example manifest (pseudo-JSON block as a single-line string in doc):
{
  "id":"m-2026-02-10-01",
  "seq":42,
  "targets":"tag:edge-staging and not tag:low-memory",
  "directives":[
    {"prewarm":{"model":"gptx-small","warm_tokens":256,"quant_profile":"a8"}},
    {"route_hint":{"upstream":"private-cluster-a","fallback_chain":["hosted-api","regional-proxy"]}}
  ],
  "rollout":{"strategy":"canary","percent":10},
  "created_by":"priya.n",
  "created_ts":"2026-02-10T09:32:00Z"
}

Sync and delta mechanics (notes):
- Broker stores manifest history; runners periodically poll /manifests?since=seq or open stream for long-poll updates.
- To save bytes, broker can send a compact delta: list of manifest ids + binary-diff patch for directive arrays.
- Runners ack with last_applied_seq; controller can compute convergence percent for rollout.

Telemetry and health:
- Heartbeat ping every 15s when online; Broker emits aggregated health for controller dashboards.
- Sample telemetry fields: cpu_pct, gpu_mem_free_mb, kv_hit_rate, avg_token_latency_ms.

Security model (sketch):
- All control messages signed by control-plane KMS key.
- Lease tokens are ephemeral JWTs signed by Broker; runners must present tokens when claiming sharded resources.
- Sensitive directives (route_hint to private cluster) require RBAC scope in manifest (created_by role check).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should runners accept manifests pushed (push) or only poll (pull)? Push reduces latency but needs persistent channels.
- How big should directives be? (We can keep them small and point to blobstore for large payloads.)
- Conflict resolution for leases when network partition causes overlapping ownership. Use last-writer-wins with lease TTL and replayable tokens?
- How do we express per-tenant limits in a mix of multi-tenant edge pools? A tenant selector in manifest might be necessary.

Implementation experiment plan (next steps):
- PoC: implement Broker + simple Runner poll path that supports manifest seq and manifest diff. (1 week)
- Extend Runner with prewarm shim that accepts prewarm directive and runs in dry-run mode (no model load). (1 week)
- Add canary rollout flags and controller view for % convergence metrics. (1 week)

Rough TODOs (personal):
- [ ] decide push vs pull default (draft prefers pull with optional stream).
- [ ] small protobuf schema sketch for RunnerAdvertise, Manifest, Lease.
- [ ] add signed token format example (JWT claims + recommended signing alg).
- [ ] wire up a tiny simulation to validate rollout percent -> convergence across flaky runners.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep selectors textual for now; if we add complex logic, bring an expression evaluator lib but avoid heavy dependencies on runners.
- Consider reusing existing runtime capability tags (see internal cap-catalog).

References / inspiration:
- internal: agent-prefetch and kv-shard-manager (search repo)
- external: Consul intent and Nomad job rollouts (conceptual)

Last thoughts:
This is intentionally small and opinionated: manifests + minimal leases + capability tags. Would like feedback from SRE/serving on how leases overlap with existing shard managers. If we go forward, the proto should be compact (<= 1KB typical small manifest) and easy to implement in SDKs.

End of scratchpad.
